summary:
## Idea
A deterministic two-dimensional spatial index over integer coordinates, with nearest/k-nearest, radius and rectangle queries. Nearest/radius ties use (squared distance, X, Y, input index); rectangle results use (X,Y,input index).

## Complexity
This builder sorts each recursive segment: O(n log² n) build work and O(n) retained storage. Queries prune subtrees but can visit O(n); do not promise worst-case logarithmic nearest search.

## Use when
Static point sets need exact integer-distance spatial queries within the supported coordinate range.

## Avoid when
Frequent inserts/removals or coordinates outside [-16383,16383] are required.

## Pitfalls
Stored and query coordinates must stay within [-16383,16383]; radius must be 0..46340. These bounds keep squared distance within int32. Duplicate points remain distinct by input index. Equal distance alone does not imply insertion order: X and Y break ties first.

## F# usage
Package: FS.GG.Algorithms; cited source API (resolve your actual package pin).
`FS.GG.Algorithms.Spatial.KdTree.build: (int * int * 'T) list -> KdTree<'T>`

```fsharp
open FS.GG.Algorithms.Spatial
let index = KdTree.build [0, 0, "home"; 3, 4, "shop"]
let nearest = KdTree.nearest 1 1 index
```

## Tests
KdTreeTests: brute-force nearest/k-nearest/radius/rectangle oracles, coordinate extremes, 100000 collinear and duplicate points.

## Bench
The cited archived 0.2.0 baseline contains spatial/kd-tree/nearest-1000-queries. Read its source commit, host/date/toolchain, sizes, work counts, runtime-specific median/p95 and spread. These are GitHub-hosted runner-class comparisons, not quiet-host absolute performance; this later source revision is not itself remeasured.
